text: Quantum computers will one day forge the signatures that guard every crypto wallet today. Magen is a wallet built for that day. Get it from the site, for Chrome or for iPhone.
Load the Chrome extension, and open it. It's the same wallet in your browser, with a live demo account to look around.
On iPhone, the app opens to the same wallet.
Now create a wallet. Pick a name. Then twelve words: your one backup, for every chain.
Those twelve words make your address on Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Solana and Cosmos, plus a quantum safe key, M L D S A sixty five.
One transaction gives the new account two locks on Near: your key, and the quantum safe one. Review it, and approve.
On the explorer: the wallet contract, deployed with both keys.
Ten test Near from the testnet helper, and every chain's address, from one seed.
Now a wallet I've used all day. Unlock it with its password.
Bring Bitcoin in. This is the wallet's own Bitcoin deposit address. Two deposits arrived, and each was minted as n B T C on Near.
Here is the mint on Near, and the Bitcoin payment it came from, sent earlier from a testnet wallet.
Zcash works the same way. A testnet deposit to this address became n Z E C on Near.
Swap half a Near for U S D T on Ref Finance. The approval shows everything: network, signer, four calls in one batch, and two signatures, classical and quantum safe.
The Near network checked both signatures before the swap ran.
Bridge out, to this wallet's own Solana address, through the Omni bridge. Same approval, same two signatures. Approve, and the bridge relays it.
It starts on the Near network, and lands on Solana's dev net.
Private send. Pay someone without linking the payment to their account. The money goes to a one time account that only they can open.
On chain, it's a payment to a fresh account, nothing more.
Back on the new wallet. Lose your phone, and guardians can help: any two of three can move your locks to a new device. Setting them up is signed twice, too.
And when classical keys stop being safe, flip the Q Day switch. It adds your quantum safe key to the account itself, as a native Near key.
The Near network now lists a post quantum key on this account, and the explorer marks it quantum safe.
The iPhone app carries the same two locks. Send shows exactly what you sign, and both signatures, before anything leaves the phone. Approve, and Near verifies both.
Here's that payment on the explorer.
One seed. Every chain. A quantum safe lock on every move, and real bridges in and out. That's Magen, on Near testnet today.
